name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data on false positives, merge conflicts, and team friction without disrupting workflows. The trade-off is delayed automation benefits, but we avoid breaking builds or frustrating contributors. After two weeks, we’ll have hard numbers to decide if parallel mode on new contributors only is worth the risk.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It won’t flag rework or missed improvements because it only sees what *doesn’t* break builds—meaning the team still inherits technical debt. Instead, run a parallel pilot where PR-Agent auto-applies *only* low-risk changes (e.g., formatting, docs) for one week, then compare the false positive/negative rates against shadow mode. The deciding factor is whether the auto-applied changes reduce reviewer workload *without* increasing rework—measure that directly.
